emails.subject: Today 10:00: inference serving decision (agenda inside)
emails.body: The inference serving decision meeting is {today} at 10:00 UTC. Compare NVIDIA NIM and vLLM for Llama 3.1 8B on L40S GPUs. Review throughput, tail latency, security sign-off, platform readiness and cost. Bring the technology report. The evaluation retrospective is {wednesday} at 14:00 UTC; bring findings and open actions.

emails.subject: Final benchmark results at 64 users - vLLM ~3.4k tokens/s, NIM ~3.1k tokens/s
emails.body: At 64 concurrent users, the fictional benchmark for Llama 3.1 8B on L40S GPUs reported vLLM at 3400 tokens/s and NIM at 3100 tokens/s. p95 latency was 2.3 seconds for vLLM and 1.6 seconds for NIM. These are synthetic demo figures, not measured product comparisons. NIM has the tighter tail latency; vLLM has higher throughput.

emails.subject: Security sign-off: both serving options approved (with rollback condition)
emails.body: Both serving options have security sign-off. NIM uses cosign-verified images; vLLM uses signed pipeline builds. Keep the old endpoint up for one week behind the same internal service name and support rollback within 15 minutes. Sam owns the final rollout security review on {wednesday} at 16:00 UTC. Bring the rollout and rollback plan plus audit evidence.

emails.subject: Decision: NVIDIA NIM for the support bot - mainly for tighter tail latency
emails.body: Decision: use NVIDIA NIM for the support bot and retain vLLM for batch workloads. The target is OpenShift AI model serving with an internal-only staging endpoint. NIM with the existing AI Enterprise subscription costs about 6% more in this fictional scenario, so cost does not decide it. Jordan owns the Acme customer update due Friday, {friday}; feedback on the draft is requested by 15:00 UTC.

emails.subject: Production load-test plan (draft) - 2 days shadow traffic, then 10%, 50%, 100% of Acme traffic
emails.body: Marco owns the production load-test plan, due Monday, {monday}. Run two days of shadow traffic, then move through 10%, 50% and 100% of Acme traffic. Include rollout dates in the customer update and retain the rollback condition.

emails.subject: Platform: production namespace request filed - 4 GPUs now, 8 once the L40S expansion lands
emails.body: Lena owns production namespace and quota preparation, due Tuesday, {tuesday}. The request is filed for 4 GPUs now and 8 once the L40S expansion lands. Finance approved the expansion quote; the purchase order goes out tomorrow and nodes are expected in 3-4 weeks. The quarterly GPU-cluster access review closes Monday, {monday}; confirm the team access list.

chat: Marco: Cost check: at our expected load, NIM with the existing AI Enterprise subscription works out ~6% more than self-built vLLM. Small enough not to decide it.
Priya: Agreed. Proposal for the meeting: go with NIM for the support bot now, keep vLLM as the option for batch workloads later.
Sam: No objection from security. One ask: the rollout plan should include a rollback to the current setup within 15 minutes.
Lena: Rollback is easy on our side: the old endpoint stays up for a week behind the same internal service name.
Marco: I'll write the load-test plan for production: 2 days of shadow traffic, then 10%, 50%, 100%.
Priya: Decision meeting done: we're going with NVIDIA NIM for the support bot. Thanks everyone. Action items in the thread.

Priya: Action items: (1) Marco: production load-test plan by Monday. (2) Lena: production namespace and quotas by Tuesday. (3) Jordan: Acme update on Friday. (4) Sam: final security review of the rollout plan by Wednesday.
Jordan: Draft Acme update is in the team folder. Feedback by 3pm please, I want to send it first thing Friday.

Lena: Production namespace request is filed. Quota: 4 GPUs now, 8 once the L40S expansion lands.
Priya: On the L40S expansion: finance approved the quote this afternoon. PO goes out tomorrow, nodes expected in 3-4 weeks.

Priya: Great work all. Retro for the evaluation next Wednesday 14:00, invite coming. Have a good evening!
